invariants: A source file is never changed by a registry operation.

A heterogeneous document intake is previewed as one disclosed batch and applied only after one explicit owner confirmation; every applied item keeps its declared role as unreviewed context until the document is read.

An AsIsSnapshot is immutable and versioned, contains exact evidence and unresolved gaps as of its capture time, admits a document version only after complete reading and fact extraction, and remains separate from the accepted BaselineSnapshot that describes what is to be implemented.
Owner acceptance of an AsIsSnapshot confirms use of the disclosed snapshot as working context and does not upgrade uncertain source facts into verified physical facts.

An AnalysisRequest is persisted independently of a chat task; every revision preserves the original request text, type and request time, a new revision may resume it after new evidence arrives, and a completed result identifies the context snapshots and output paths actually used.
A document is not fully read unless its exact indexed version has a complete ReadingRun without unresolved coverage gaps.
A complete ReadingRun proves physical coverage of a document but does not by itself prove complete semantic extraction; that requires a complete FactExtractionRun for the same exact version.
A source document is stored once; its facts may belong to multiple disciplines, project packages, sites, zones and systems without copying the original.
A ProjectPackage is a bounded analysis and delivery scope, not a physical folder and not a substitute for Site, Zone or System.
An InformationGap blocks only the conclusions and decisions listed as dependent on it; independent checks remain available.
A CoordinationRun is complete only when every declared package pair, shared-resource demand and known interface in its scope was checked and every detected issue was recorded.
Every decision-facing conclusion is linked to registered facts, calculations, normative references, findings or information gaps; unsupported free text is not a decision basis.
A complete ReadingRun uses expected units from a current DocumentInventory for the same document version and SHA-256; self-declared coverage alone is insufficient.
A complete ReadingRun records every visual, OCR, hidden-content, formula, or embedded-part requirement declared by its current DocumentInventory as checked.
A proposal never becomes part of a BaselineSnapshot merely because it was received or analyzed.
Owner acceptance of a BaselineSnapshot is an explicit OwnerDecision and remains separate from technical approval and official approval of each selected document.

A BaselineSnapshot is immutable and versioned; changing selected document versions, scope, conflict treatment or atomic requirements creates a new snapshot linked through supersedes_baseline_snapshot_id.

Every document version selected into a BaselineSnapshot has a complete ReadingRun for the exact indexed version, a stated project role and applicability scope, and contributes at least one atomic ApprovedRequirement with a precise source locator.

A contractor proposal, an automatically selected older version, an external reference, an invoice, a photograph or another document without project requirements is not admitted to the baseline without an explicit owner decision and extracted requirement evidence; a Quote source is never admitted.
Statement kind, evidence origin and verification status are recorded independently.
Asset lifecycle status, operational status and dated condition are separate dimensions and are not substituted for one another.
Normative compliance and evidence of actual practice are separate findings.
An alternative is not suitable until its mandatory baseline requirements and total comparable cost have been checked.
A comparable is not used in a benchmark calculation until the owner has confirmed its relevance after the known differences were shown.
An address, coordinate, map zone or installed position is recorded only with a stated source and precision.
The absence of a registered hidden route or physical element is not evidence that it is absent and cannot by itself make drilling, cutting or other intrusive work safe.
Installed-asset history is append-only; the current state is derived from verified events and assessments rather than erasing prior states.

A concrete physical unit is registered as an Asset only after its acquisition, acceptance or other individual inventory registration is evidenced; before that the product or option remains an EquipmentOption, Alternative, Comparable or quote subject, and installation and commissioning are recorded as separate events.
A completed AssetEvent represents an occurred event, while future work remains a MaintenancePlan or WorkRequest.
A maintenance due date is calculated only from a sourced rule and a verified base event or meter reading; otherwise it remains unknown.
Age alone does not determine replacement; condition, failures, supportability, compatibility, consequences and lifecycle cost are evaluated separately.
A replacement candidate is not suitable until mounting, space, power, data, control, environmental, software, service and regulatory interfaces have been checked where applicable.
A change to an operating object is assessed against the target location, physical elements, hidden routes, connected systems and dependent assets before work is recommended.
Manufacturer lifetime, maintenance interval and end-of-support statements remain sourced claims and are not treated as observed condition.
A LifecycleCostAssessment states its horizon, usage scenario, currency, included components and unknown components; a missing amount is never treated as zero.
A PriceObservation is a dated observation for a stated seller, region, currency, tax, delivery and availability context and is not an evergreen current price.

A NormReference records the exact designation, title, edition, document kind, official status, jurisdiction, territory, check date, official status source, direct source URL and declared scope; document status alone does not establish applicability to a particular object.
A RegulatoryRequirement represents one normalized requirement with an exact clause locator and verification method; it does not silently import the whole normative document.

A complete ComplianceAssessment covers every declared expected requirement exactly once through linked ComplianceResult records and keeps mandatory, project, contract, reference-only and undetermined applicability separate.
A conformity statement is not made from a document title alone: the applicable clause, target, evidence, check date and result are recorded, while missing inputs block only dependent conclusions.
A RegulatorySyncRun detects source or status changes but never accepts a new edition, changes applicability or rewrites a prior ComplianceAssessment automatically.
A Quote identifies exactly one commercial counterparty: a Contractor or a Supplier.

A ProposalReview is an immutable revision tied to one exact Quote and source-document version; a new conclusion creates the next revision in the same series and links the immediately preceding revision.

A ProposalReview explicitly records whether it uses current factual state, an owner-accepted baseline, both, or documents only; it never substitutes project intent for observed state or observed state for accepted requirements.

When factual context is used, every source fact of the selected current AsIsSnapshot is classified exactly once; when an accepted baseline is used, every requirement of the selected BaselineSnapshot is classified exactly once as applicable, not applicable or undetermined.
A ProposalReview classifies every quote item and records baseline_assessment_mode as accepted_baseline, reference_only or no_relevant_documents.

Only accepted_baseline mode may claim conformance to an owner-accepted baseline; it records the applied scope and covers every selected applicable requirement, while reference_only comparisons are labelled separately and do not create ApprovedRequirement records.
Missing baseline inputs block only dependent conformance, quantity, cost or contract-readiness conclusions and do not block independent proposal checks or reference comparison.

A current ProposalReview satisfies the current proposal-review contract: every universal check, every required axis for each declared discipline, every technical-alternative track and every foreman section has an explicit evidence-linked result; additional_model_checks remains open for model-discovered analysis.
A legacy ProposalReview remains historical under its recorded contract version and is not silently presented as satisfying the current contract.
A ProposalReview cannot be ready_for_owner while a required contract item is blocked, requires specialist work, lacks evidence-quality fields, or is absent from its completion_manifest.

Every registered review Alternative is compared on the same required axes against project requirements, factual state, performance, interfaces, constructability, regulation, cost, schedule, lifecycle and owner criteria.

A price comparison states normalized scope, quantity, currency, tax, delivery, installation, observation date and region; an unknown or non-comparable price remains an explicit limitation and is not used as a market analogue.
Every linked InformationGap becomes one structured clarification with recipient, evidence request, response format, priority, blocked conclusion, answer status and verification evidence.

Before a recommendation, ProposalReview records the strongest counterargument, plausible failure modes and evidence that could change the recommendation; insufficient evidence blocks decision readiness.

ready_for_negotiation and ready_for_contract are different decision-readiness states; the latter additionally requires closed contract-stage site checks and clarifications, no blocking context conflict or cost exposure, a fully evidenced contractor assessment, and ready CostPlan and SchedulePlan revisions for the preferred scenario.

A completed technical-alternative track links a real Alternative and records performance, cost and constructability bases; an alternative contractor using the same solution does not satisfy a different technical principle.

A current ready_for_owner ProposalReview identifies at least one potentially comparable or quote-required commercial party different from the quoted party; the quoted party cannot satisfy its own alternative search.
A technical check or calculation never invents a required value; each input is sourced or explicitly unknown, and specialist review remains a valid outcome.
External search records exclude private project details that are not necessary for the query and preserve the query, date, region and checked source URLs.
LifecycleDecision is an analytical record: recommendation_ready and awaiting_owner_decision do not authorize work or purchase.
LifecycleDecision with status recommendation_ready or awaiting_owner_decision records its conclusion as statement_kind recommendation.
LifecycleDecision status owner_decided requires an explicit linked OwnerDecision, and status implemented additionally requires implementation evidence.
EquipmentOption status selected and WorkRequest status approved require an explicit linked OwnerDecision.
A Supplier or Contractor found in external sources remains a candidate until its identity, scope, conditions and comparability have been checked.
A CostPlan is an immutable revision whose total is reproducible from atomic items; unknown amounts remain explicit and prevent ready_for_baseline status rather than becoming zero.

A SchedulePlan is an immutable revision whose activities, dependencies, calendars, constraints and date bases are explicit; calculated dates and criticality are not claimed while required durations or dependencies are unknown.

A ManagementBaseline is created only by an explicit OwnerDecision and binds one exact ready CostPlan revision to one exact ready SchedulePlan revision under the same accepted project BaselineSnapshot and the same complete work_item_id set.
An approved change does not silently rewrite an accepted ManagementBaseline; its cost and schedule impact is recorded separately and a changed baseline requires a new owner-accepted version.
A ControlSnapshot is immutable and dated; physical progress, contractual completion, acceptance, payment and operational readiness remain separate states.
Cost and schedule forecasts show their formulas, exact baseline, approved changes, actual data, remaining estimate and unknown exposure; missing values are not treated as zero.
Plan-fact and earned-value indicators are calculated only from an explicit weighting basis and evidence-backed actuals; an indicator never substitutes for inspection, acceptance or payment evidence.
